summary: Oak View sits in the Ojai Valley along the Ventura River, wedged between the Topatopa Mountains to the north and the coastal range to the south — a setting where 9.6 hours of daily sunshine pour into a narrow inland corridor that routinely runs five to ten degrees warmer than the coast just twelve miles away, pushing average daytime highs to a dry 72°F. At just 3.4 square miles and under 6,000 people, it functions largely as a bedroom community; most employment draws from the healthcare, agriculture, hospitality, and public-sector jobs scattered between Ojai proper and the city of Ventura, meaning a commute along Highway 33 or Highway 150 is the daily norm. A median home value of $709,300 against a median household income near $110,000 yields a price-to-income ratio above 6.4, which puts outright purchasing out of comfortable reach for a household earning around the median — and median rent at $2,463 claims a significant share of monthly take-home. The tradeoff is tangible proximity to the Los Padres National Forest and the network of trails climbing into the backcountry directly from the valley floor. Oak View is essentially a small residential wedge that borrows its grandeur from the geography surrounding it, not from anything built within its own borders.
